uiGlyphs.defect_found_and_repaired: 2026-10-17, same day. glyphs-24.mjs ran ONE even-odd polygon pass over every ring from every <path> in a source icon. SVG fills each <path> independently and unions them, so on a multi-path icon a later path carved holes in an earlier one. Verified by rasterising both the original SVG and our encoding to a 24x24 canvas in the browser and diffing pixel by pixel (scripts/glyph-diff.mjs): leave lost 4px, useItem 8px, flag 8px, withdrawal 8px. Every single-path glyph diffed at 0, which is what isolated the cause. Fixed the builder to fill per path then union, and re-shipped the 11 affected instances in the handoff via scripts/glyphs-refill.mjs (matches by pixel set, preserves each instance's own fill, refuses to write if any buggy set survives or tags go unbalanced). Post-fix diff: 0 of 12 differ from the browser render. Lesson: a gate that checks palette, orphans and contrast cannot see a wrong FILL RULE — the only check that catches it is comparing against an independent renderer of the source.
uiGlyphs.fillRuleDefect: 2026-10-17, same day as the ship. See the defect_found_and_repaired note above. Two more glyphs (update, alert) were added afterwards and are multi-path or verified: arrow-up is also 2-path and would have lost 8px to the old order.
uiGlyphs.provenanceGate: scripts/glyph-provenance.mjs re-derives every sourced glyph from its vendored SVG and exits non-zero on drift. 13 sourced verified, 1 hand-drawn, 0 drift.

motionSpec.revised: 2026-10-30, second revision. Sections 4 and 6 of the art bible.
motionSpec.whySecondRevision: The first revision of each was written against assets-raw/turn-states.html, a scratch page I had authored from the spec. The handoff already contained a working motion vocabulary that contradicted almost every value. Same error twice: describing the artefact from a model of it instead of reading it.
motionSpec.authoritativeRead: scripts/motion-vocabulary.mjs — dumps every @keyframes, timing token, animation-bearing class and demo function out of Savborne-handoff.html. Run it before amending section 4 or 6.

correctedFromTheDocument.lunge: 0 -> translateX(24px) -> 0, 450ms steps(6). I had specified 0 -> -3 -> +9 -> 0 at ease-out.
correctedFromTheDocument.damage: .sv-hit is filter:brightness(2.2) 400ms steps(4) PLUS sv-shake +-6px 300ms steps(5). I had specified a #FF706D colour tint, which the document has never implemented.
correctedFromTheDocument.hpDrain: sv-fill 700ms steps(14). I had specified 500ms linear.
correctedFromTheDocument.thinkingIndicator: sv-dots exists (width 0 -> 2ch). My first draft claimed no thinking indicator can work under polling; a HELD indicator works fine, an instantaneous one does not.
correctedFromTheDocument.alsoMissed: sv-enter, sv-pop, sv-tick, sv-levelup, and the token set --sv-ease, --sv-t-press, --sv-t-enter, --sv-t-fill, --sv-t-pop

motionSpec.houseRule: Motion is quantised. Every battle and feedback beat uses steps(n), not a smooth ease. Only sv-pop and sv-enter use --sv-ease, and they are transitions rather than state.
motionSpec.scopeNarrowed: Section 4 now governs only the two battle sprites and their nameplates. General UI motion is transition and feedback and is free of the one-channel-one-meaning rule. It had already broken that rule four times: sv-tick and sv-levelup use scale, sv-enter and sv-pop use vertical offset, sv-shake uses horizontal offset, and damage uses a filter rather than a tint.
motionSpec.channelIsGesture: A channel is a perceptual gesture, not a CSS property. Lunge and shake both animate translateX and both are legitimate because they are distinguishable without reading - one-way and committed versus two-way and decaying.

pendingWork.timeoutBeat: Needs an API change. The server auto-plays defend on deadline and the payload reports it as a chosen move, so the client cannot tell them apart. Needs an auto / move_source flag on the move row, surfaced through the battle GET.
pendingWork.glowBeat: Needs a pre-baked 8-neighbour gilt rim path per character in assets/characters.json. Not done. A 4-neighbour rim renders as a dotted outline. filter: drop-shadow would break the quantised idiom. Until it lands, defend and item-use have no animation.
pendingWork.arenasWithoutPlates: A_ItemSheet, A_Win, A_Loss and A_Tie carry no nameplate, so handover and commit beats have nowhere to land.

motionSpec.reducedMotion: Implemented twice in the document and both are required: a CSS media query, and a JS reduce flag from matchMedia used inside the demo functions. The media query alone cannot express "skip this beat but still drain the bar".

faces.Silkscreen: 20px and above — titles, wordmark, display numerals at 20px or more, whether or not the value changes. No OpenType features at all, so it can never carry tabular figures.
faces.Plus Jakarta Sans: below 20px — body, labels, and every figure that updates below 20px.

typography.rejected: Space Mono for numerals — a fourth download on a zero-budget mobile app, competing with Silkscreen for the same role. Tabular figures are a feature, not a typeface.
typography.headers: Uppercase with letter-spacing, as shipped. Sentence case was recommended and overruled by the user; recorded as their call.
typography.bugFixed: .num was applied in 14 places across 7 files and defined nowhere. HP readouts, Turn X of Y, the auto-defend countdown, the NIM balance, XP totals and leaderboard scores all rendered in proportional figures and re-flowed width as values changed.
typography.fix: src/app/globals.css gains a .num utility pinning the family to Jakarta and enabling tabular figures. tsc --noEmit clean.
typography.verifiedNotAssumed: font-variant-numeric is a silent no-op without a tnum feature, so scripts/font-features.mjs Brotli-decompresses the self-hosted woff2 and reads the feature tags. Result: Jakarta latin subset HAS tnum and pnum; two secondary Jakarta subsets do not; all four Silkscreen cuts have no OpenType features at all.
typography.watchFor: Digits are U+0030-0039, inside the latin unicode-range, so the tabulating cut is the one that serves them. Re-run font-features.mjs after any font or subset change, or numerals can silently go proportional again.

measured.method: Live DOM at 24px after document.fonts.ready, each digit's width read individually and fonts confirmed loaded with document.fonts.check. Canvas measureText was tried first and discarded — it cannot apply font-variant-numeric, so it reported Jakarta tnum as an 8.21px spread when the DOM measures it flat at 0.00.
measured.silkscreenDigits: NOT uniform: '1' advances 15.00px, every other digit 18.00px — a 3.00px spread. The art bible's claim that Silkscreen digits are uniform because it is a pixel font was false, and is corrected.
measured.grid: Silkscreen advance widths are whole pixels at 12/16/20/24/28/32/36/40/44/48 and fractional at 14/18/21/26/29/30/51, so a Silkscreen size that is not a multiple of 4 is a bug. text-3xl (30px) is the one shipped size that is off the grid.
measured.boundary: The 20px line decides who may own display; it is not a ban on Jakarta at size. Reading text — paragraphs, labels, status lines — stays Jakarta at any size.
measured.counts: Before pass 1 the artefact held 47 Silkscreen instances below 20px and 21 at or above, plus 60 Jakarta at 20px or more.

pass3.numberingRule: Silkscreen draws display and numerals at 20px and up; Jakarta draws everything below 20px, numerals included. One face per size. This corrects the pass-2 behaviour split (a number that changes value is Jakarta's), which put the ticking 28px queue timer and the 24px +20 XP in different faces by design. A display numeral at 20px or more is Silkscreen whether or not its value ticks.

typography.numScope: Corrected 2026-11-02: .num applies to updating figures BELOW 20px only. A numeral at 20px or more is Silkscreen by the pass-3 size rule, and .num on Silkscreen is a silent no-op because it has no tnum feature. The NIM balance is 36px Silkscreen in the artefact, so it is not a .num site in the design of record.
typography.balanceBuildGap: The app renders the balance as .num text-3xl (Jakarta 30px) in src/app/(tabs)/page.tsx. That is a build gap, not a typography decision — it is also the one shipped size off the 4px grid — recorded here the way the 44px->24px result titles are.
